# std.fs

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Filesystem access. Operations run on the blocking pool and park the
calling task instead of blocking the worker.

## Types

### `Dir`

```badger
struct Dir { root: String }
```

Authority over one directory tree: paths are relative to it, and none
(absolute, `..`, or through a symlink) reaches outside it. Only `root`
and `Dir.sub` make one, so a function given a `Dir` can touch that tree
and nothing else through it; `reader` narrows it to reading.

### `File`

```badger
struct File { handle: native.Handle }
```

An open file: an `io.Reader` and `io.Writer` (as its mode allows).
Closed by `close`, or once nothing can reach it.

#### `File.close`

```badger
fn close(self: &Self) -> Result<Unit, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

Flush and close; later reads and writes fail with `:io/closed`.

### `Metadata`

```badger
pub type Metadata = { kind: Symbol, size: Int, modified_nanos: Int, readonly: Bool }
```

What is at a path: `:file`, `:dir`, `:symlink` (not followed), or
`:other`, with its size in bytes and when it last changed.
